name: Knowledge Lab
title: Enterprise knowledge assistant & evaluation lab
headline: Answers you can trace back to evidence.
summary: Explore a fictional knowledge base, inspect citations and compare retrieval decisions. Optional local Ollama inference adds a separately validated model draft.
runtime: React + TypeScript; optional Python / LangChain / Ollama
goal: Help a support team find a supported answer while making source conflicts, missing evidence and access boundaries visible.

capabilities.title: Inspect exact evidence
capabilities.description: Read source passages, document owners, dates and rendered citations rather than accepting an unexplained answer.

capabilities.title: Compare retrieval behaviour
capabilities.description: Compare a keyword baseline with governed BM25 retrieval, source-status filters, role filters and coverage guards.

capabilities.title: Exercise difficult questions
capabilities.description: Try contradictory documents, undocumented topics and a restricted synthetic record. Inspect why the system answers or abstains.

capabilities.title: Evaluate and extend
capabilities.description: Rerun labelled development and verification cases, inspect recorded model reviews, or import a custom JSON knowledge pack.

instructions.title: Open a support question
instructions.description: Open the public demo and choose Support target. Read the quoted answer, then open its citation to inspect the original passage.

instructions.title: Change the retrieval rules
instructions.description: Switch between governed retrieval and the keyword baseline. Compare which draft, archived or authoritative sources appear.

instructions.title: Test the boundaries
instructions.description: Choose Conflicting sources, Missing answer and Restricted record. Compare the support and administrator demo roles.

instructions.title: Inspect the evaluation
instructions.description: Open Evaluation lab and compare the development and verification sets across all six configurations. Custom packs disable the sample labels.

instructions.title: Try local inference if wanted
instructions.description: Follow the repository setup, run npm run dev:local with Ollama and qwen3:8b installed, then expand Optional local inference and check the service before drafting an answer.

decisions.title: Evidence before generation
decisions.description: Public evidence mode quotes canonical passages and runs entirely in the browser. It is useful without a model account or a hosted inference service.

decisions.title: Server-owned context admission
decisions.description: The optional loopback Python adapter reloads the canonical pack, applies its own role and validates admitted context before calling Ollama.

decisions.title: Keep measured claims bounded
decisions.description: The synthetic cases expose regressions and model errors. Passing them does not establish general accuracy or independent human acceptance.

limits: All company policies and records are synthetic. Browser role filtering over a public pack is a simulation, not private-data protection.
The public demo does not run hosted model inference. Ollama runs only in the optional local checkout.
Both labelled sets are agent-authored regression coverage. Version 1 was accepted on agent validation; human review is not claimed.
evidence: 68 recorded retrieval/pipeline cases and 46 generated-answer content checks pass in the accepted local Qwen3 8B run.
Seven invalid-context probes are rejected. Earlier retrieval and model failures remain in the repository.
Source-linked agent review and reproducible setup are published with the project.

board.note: The upper path is the public browser demo. The lower-right branch runs only when the optional local service is configured.

name: Integration Lab
title: Integration & webhook reliability lab
headline: A failed delivery should leave a useful trail.
summary: Send signed synthetic events through real HTTP, inject receiver failures and recover with visible retries, deduplication and dead-letter history.
runtime: React; public Worker / D1; local ASP.NET Core / SQLite
mode: Real HTTP, explicit virtual retry clock
goal: Help an operator determine what failed, whether an order effect already committed and how to recover without duplicating it.

capabilities.title: Inject controlled failures
capabilities.description: Exercise outages, throttling, invalid signatures, expired timestamps, bad payloads and a lost response after a successful commit.

capabilities.title: Inspect the delivery history
capabilities.description: Follow correlation IDs, raw HTTP outcomes, retry deadlines, attempt cycles and the order-effect ledger.

capabilities.title: Recover safely
capabilities.description: Replay a dead letter, repair the synthetic sender and confirm that retries and duplicate events retain one effect.

capabilities.title: Compare real runtimes
capabilities.description: The public Worker/D1 API and runnable ASP.NET Core/SQLite reference implement the same contract and acceptance scenarios.

instructions.title: Run an outage
instructions.description: Select Run outage scenario. Four actual HTTP requests fail while the explicitly virtual retry clock advances by 5, 15 and 45 seconds.

instructions.title: Inspect the dead letter
instructions.description: Open its correlation ID, attempt responses and order ledger. Confirm that the failed delivery has not created an order effect.

instructions.title: Restore the receiver
instructions.description: Select Healthy, then Replay & repair sender and Send next attempt. The receipt and one order effect are committed while failed history remains.

instructions.title: Send the duplicate
instructions.description: Select Queue duplicate and send it. Inspect the cached success and confirm that the order ledger still has one effect.

instructions.title: Test uncertain delivery
instructions.description: On a new order, select Lose response after committing. Retry after advancing the clock and verify that the already committed effect is not duplicated.

decisions.title: Commit the outcome together
decisions.description: Receipt, order effect, delivery status and audit transition commit in one optimistic SQL update. A concurrent loser reloads and recomputes.

decisions.title: Keep retries inspectable
decisions.description: Backoff, Retry-After handling and replay are explicit state transitions. Operators can see why an event is due, rejected or in dead letters.

decisions.title: Use a fixed receiver
decisions.description: The browser posts a reserved signed envelope to one controlled receiver endpoint. The session signing secret is not returned to the browser.

limits: Events, orders and failure modes are synthetic. Outages and lost responses are intentional fault injection.
The sender runs in the browser and uses explicit virtual retry time. Deliveries do not continue after the tab closes.
The demo does not claim production throughput, an uptime guarantee or distributed exactly-once delivery.
evidence: Shared HTTP acceptance checks exercise the real .NET and Worker APIs, persistence, session expiry and concurrent updates.
Published validation covers rejected authentication, replay, deduplication and lost-response recovery.
The source includes the contract, state model, retained failures and an operator runbook.

board.note: The browser delivers a reserved envelope to a fixed receiver. Retry scheduling uses an explicitly advanced virtual clock; it is not a background queue.

zones.title: PUBLIC WORKER + D1 / EQUIVALENT LOCAL .NET API

nodes.subtitle: Browser HTTP sender

nodes.title: Synthetic sender API

nodes.title: Fixed HTTP receiver
nodes.subtitle: HMAC + idempotency
nodes.detail: The receiver checks timestamp, signature, raw bytes, event identity and order version before committing an effect.

nodes.title: Atomic SQL outcome
nodes.subtitle: Receipt + one effect
nodes.detail: The optimistic update commits the receipt, business effect, attempt status and audit transition together.

nodes.title: Virtual retry clock
nodes.subtitle: Backoff / Retry-After
nodes.detail: The operator explicitly advances virtual time. A retry uses the recorded deadline rather than an invisible timer.

nodes.title: Dead-letter review
nodes.subtitle: Replay + repair sender
nodes.detail: Exhausted or non-retryable work remains inspectable. Replay opens a new attempt cycle and keeps prior evidence.

nodes.title: Audit & evidence
nodes.subtitle: Attempts + safe export
nodes.detail: Correlation IDs, attempts, outcomes and the ledger can be inspected and exported without access credentials.

flows.title: Outage to recovery
flows.summary: Follow a failed delivery into dead letters, then replay it safely.

steps.title: Reserve a delivery
steps.detail: The console asks the API to claim one synthetic delivery attempt.

steps.title: Return the signed envelope
steps.detail: The API returns the reserved body and signature for the browser sender.

steps.title: Attempt actual HTTP delivery
steps.detail: The browser posts the envelope to the fixed receiver. The outage fixture returns a real 503.

steps.title: Record the retry deadline
steps.detail: The retryable failure records a deadline. The operator advances the virtual clock to inspect subsequent attempts.

steps.title: Retain the dead letter
steps.detail: After the configured attempts are exhausted, the delivery enters dead letters without an order effect.

steps.title: Restore and replay
steps.detail: The operator selects Healthy and explicitly replays the retained delivery, optionally repairing its synthetic sender fault.

steps.title: Commit one effect
steps.detail: Authentication, idempotency and version checks precede the atomic receipt and order-effect commit.

steps.title: Keep the full recovery trail
steps.detail: Failed attempts remain alongside the successful replay in the audit and exported evidence.

flows.title: Duplicate / lost-response safety
flows.summary: A retry can return success without creating another order effect.

steps.title: Send the event
steps.detail: A valid reserved envelope reaches the receiver over actual HTTP.

steps.title: Persist the original effect
steps.detail: The SQL outcome commits before the synthetic lost-response fixture returns 503 to the sender.

steps.title: Treat the response as uncertain
steps.detail: The sender schedules a retry because it did not receive success. That does not prove the business effect failed.

steps.title: Reserve the retry when due
steps.detail: The explicit clock reaches the saved deadline and another attempt is reserved.

steps.title: Deliver the same event again
steps.detail: The retry carries the same event identity and bytes.

steps.title: Return the stored result
steps.detail: Idempotency returns the original success. No second business effect is created.

steps.title: Verify the ledger
steps.detail: The attempt trail shows both outcomes while the order-effect count stays at one.

name: Presales Workbench
title: Technical presales solution workbench
headline: Turn discovery into a decision you can explain.
summary: Explore a fictional customer brief, compare feasible architecture options and produce an editable proposal with explicit assumptions, costs and a PoC plan.
runtime: React + TypeScript; browser-local calculations and drafts
mode: No model, account or backend draft store
goal: Make the relationship between customer constraints, an architectural recommendation and a proposed evaluation inspectable.

capabilities.title: Structure customer discovery
capabilities.description: Capture business goals, current systems, stakeholders, integration scope, constraints and decision ownership.

capabilities.title: Compare realistic trade-offs
capabilities.description: Three provider-neutral blueprints pass hard feasibility gates before weighted capability scores are considered.

capabilities.title: Explore cost assumptions
capabilities.description: Edit illustrative rates, traffic, peak load, growth and headroom, then inspect reconciled cost line items.

capabilities.title: Create a usable workshop pack
capabilities.description: Edit a proposal, preserve authored wording when inputs change, define measurable PoC criteria and export a seven-file ZIP.

instructions.title: Start with Northstar Retail
instructions.description: Read the fictional business goal, stakeholders, three current systems and operating constraints in Discovery.

instructions.title: Compare the baseline
instructions.description: Open Compare options. Inspect hard constraints, weighted contributions and cost lines for the managed-workflow baseline.

instructions.title: Introduce a new constraint
instructions.description: Return to Discovery and select Introduce this constraint. The new five-second delivery requirement blocks the 60-second baseline and changes the proposed direction.

instructions.title: Review the proposal
instructions.description: Open Proposal & PoC and edit a section. Change a structured input and inspect the review flag while your wording is preserved.

instructions.title: Export and continue
instructions.description: Download the proposal pack, extract brief.json and re-import it to continue the workshop. Try the other fictional scenarios to explore different boundaries.

decisions.title: Feasibility before scoring
decisions.description: An attractive score cannot override a hard boundary, ownership, region, delivery-time or budget constraint.

decisions.title: Keep assumptions editable
decisions.description: Rates, latency baselines, capability ratings and delivery allowances remain visible workshop assumptions. Currency is a label, not an exchange-rate conversion.

decisions.title: Preserve authored judgement
decisions.description: A changed brief flags proposal text for review rather than silently replacing the user's wording with a regenerated draft.

limits: Customers, rates, capability ratings and requirements are fictional workshop fixtures.
Exports are proposed drafts and future PoC acceptance criteria, not a completed PoC, binding quotation or delivery commitment.
Drafts remain in this browser origin. Export before switching scenarios or clearing browser storage; no server-side draft store or AI inference is used.
evidence: 48 unit tests and 12 scenario/export checks are published, covering six baseline/changed-constraint decisions.
Recorded checks independently reconcile cost totals, budget boundaries, ZIP extraction and JSON round trips.
Windows/Linux CI, public browser checks and hosting validation are recorded in the repository.

board.note: Every decision and draft lives in the visitor's browser. The public Worker serves the application and documents, not a remote scoring or AI service.

name: Traceability Lab
title: Manufacturing data quality & traceability demonstrator
headline: Every corrected reading keeps its original story.
summary: Ingest synthetic manufacturing measurements, investigate known quality defects and follow a reviewed correction from its original source to its current overlay.
runtime: React + TypeScript; Node SQLite / public Worker D1
mode: Synthetic batches with server-enforced demo roles
goal: Help a quality team explain which process readings are trustworthy and trace every reviewed change back to its source.

capabilities.title: Reconcile the ingestion
capabilities.description: Retain raw records and reconcile usable, quarantined, duplicate and missing expected measurements.

capabilities.title: Investigate known defects
capabilities.description: Check completeness, exact and conflicting duplicates, types, units, ranges, timestamps, equipment and sampling-plan membership.

capabilities.title: Review a bounded correction
capabilities.description: Operators propose permitted field changes. Reviewer decisions check versions and findings before applying a curated overlay.

capabilities.title: Follow the evidence
capabilities.description: Inspect original/current fields, source pointers, resolved finding history, a hash-linked audit and a verifiable six-file evidence ZIP.

instructions.title: Ingest the sample run
instructions.description: Use the Operator role. Eleven source rows reconcile to four usable, five quarantined and two duplicates; eight of nine expected slots are observed.

instructions.title: Trace a finding
instructions.description: Open the UNIT finding for MES-004 in batch AX-1102. Follow the source-row pointer, inspect raw JSON and compare original/current fields.

instructions.title: Propose the correction
instructions.description: Use the fictional source-owner clarification to change degC to °C. Submission creates a proposal and leaves the measurement unchanged.

instructions.title: Review and approve
instructions.description: Switch to Reviewer, record a rationale and approve. The curated measurement becomes version 2 while the original and resolved finding remain visible.

instructions.title: Verify the trail
instructions.description: Open Audit trail and download the six-file ZIP. Optionally ingest the separate follow-up pressure reading to close AX-1103's completeness gap.

decisions.title: Retain the original
decisions.description: Corrections update a versioned overlay. Canonical source hashes, row ordinals and the original reading remain available for investigation.

decisions.title: Protect concurrent reviews
decisions.description: A mutation token and optimistic revision guard the SQL transaction. Approval also checks the proposed measurement version.

decisions.title: Verify before export
decisions.description: Export verification checks source hashes, reconciliation, audit links and proposal/decision history before producing the evidence files.

limits: All batches, readings, specifications and source-owner statements are synthetic.
One visitor can switch demo roles. This exercises server permissions, not separate verified people or independent two-person control.
The hash chain is not a digital signature. The demonstrator makes no product-release, regulatory-approval or pharmaceutical-system validation claim.
evidence: 40 unit tests and the same 24 HTTP scenarios on local SQLite, Worker/D1 and both public origins are recorded.
Local restart and public redeployment checks preserve source records, reviewed overlays, finding history and access.
Published browser validation includes actual downloads, independent verification, re-import and mobile layout.

board.note: The arrows illustrate ingestion and review steps. Demo roles belong to one visitor; approved corrections change a curated overlay while the raw source remains intact.

name: Workflow Lab
title: MCP integration & controlled workflow demo
headline: Give tools access. Keep authority explicit.
summary: Investigate synthetic orders through real MCP tools, inspect the proposed follow-up and approve one bounded, replay-safe task write.
runtime: Official MCP SDK 2.4; React; SQLite / Worker D1
mode: Deterministic runner, real MCP Streamable HTTP
goal: Let an operational investigator read useful records and propose an action without granting it the power to approve its own write.

capabilities.title: Use genuine MCP tools
capabilities.description: Discover strict schemas, look up an order, read untrusted error history and draft a deterministic follow-up over real MCP HTTP calls.

capabilities.title: Inspect the exact proposal
capabilities.description: Review the task body, fixed queue, source order version, actor, resource, payload digest and ten-minute approval window.

capabilities.title: Enforce the write boundary
capabilities.description: Separate capabilities govern reading, execution, proposal requests and review. The server rejects pending, rejected, stale, tampered and unscoped writes.

capabilities.title: Verify what happened
capabilities.description: Run five live denial probes, inspect captured protocol bodies and verify a hash-linked audit and six-file evidence export.

instructions.title: Investigate ORD-2048
instructions.description: Run Investigate order. Inspect the source errors, exact task payload and real request/response bodies in the MCP wire inspector.

instructions.title: Send the proposal for review
instructions.description: Select Send for approval. Try Execute MCP call while pending and observe the server denial. A Controller approval attempt also fails.

instructions.title: Approve the bounded action
instructions.description: Switch the demo review capability to Reviewer, enter a reason and select Approve exact task. Approval itself does not execute the write.

instructions.title: Execute and replay
instructions.description: Execute the MCP call to create the synthetic internal task. Replay the same call and confirm that it returns the existing task.

instructions.title: Challenge the boundaries
instructions.description: Run Security checks, then investigate ORD-2057's untrusted injection fixture. Download the evidence ZIP and verify its evidence.json through the file chooser.

decisions.title: Separate data from authority
decisions.description: Partner error text is displayed as untrusted evidence. A fixed template uses allowlisted identifiers and codes; retrieved text cannot grant permissions.

decisions.title: Bind approval to the exact action
decisions.description: The immutable proposal binds payload hash, workspace, actor, resource, source version and expiry. Execution revalidates every binding.

decisions.title: Commit once, replay safely
decisions.description: One optimistic SQL update consumes the approval, creates the task, advances the order version and appends its audit. Replay reads the existing task.

limits: All operational records are synthetic. The guided runner is deterministic and does not call a language model.
One visitor owns the demo capabilities and can switch roles. Verified separate identity and two-person approval are not claimed.
Manual audience-bound bearer capabilities are used. The project does not implement an OAuth authorization server or automatic ChatGPT plugin installation.
evidence: 40 unit tests and 34 HTTP scenarios per local/public target exercise audience, scope, malformed input, rejection, tampering, staleness and concurrent execution.
20 local and 14 public browser checks include actual download, independent extraction, evidence re-import and mobile layout.
Local restart and public redeployment checks retain the original capability, task, proposals and complete audit state.

board.note: This is a fixed investigator plan using real MCP. The lower lane shows a separate demo review capability, not a second verified person. Animation illustrates the design, not live server telemetry.

flows.title: Investigate, approve, execute
flows.summary: A proposed action acquires authority only through a separate explicit decision.

steps.title: Connect with read scope
steps.detail: The SDK negotiates MCP and uses the reader capability for investigation.

steps.title: Retrieve synthetic records
steps.detail: Lookup and error-history tools return data. External-looking text cannot change the tool plan or permissions.

steps.title: Build the exact task proposal
steps.detail: The deterministic template uses known identifiers and error codes, with a fixed internal queue.

steps.title: Present the proposal for review
steps.detail: The draft crosses into the review UI as a proposal, carrying no write authority.

steps.title: Use the reviewer capability
steps.detail: After requesting review, the visitor explicitly switches to Reviewer and supplies a reason to approve the exact task.

steps.title: Record the bounded approval
steps.detail: The review API stores the immutable payload and binds it to workspace, actor, resource, source version and expiry.

steps.title: Attempt the MCP write
steps.detail: The executor submits approvalId and payloadHash to create_followup. Scope alone does not authorize the task.

steps.title: Recheck and commit once
steps.detail: The policy checks every binding, consumes the approved proposal and writes one task and audit atomically. Replaying the call returns the existing task.

flows.title: An unapproved write is refused
flows.summary: Executor scope cannot turn untrusted content into approval.

steps.title: Begin with a scoped connection

steps.title: Receive the injection fixture

steps.title: Keep the fixed proposal template
steps.detail: The proposed task excludes the injected instructions and points only at the internal demo queue.

steps.title: Reject the missing approval
steps.detail: create_followup refuses an unknown or pending approval. No task or order update is committed; the denial is audited.
